issues.problem: The expected recipe set and the 80/56/8 count are both built from activeWoods(), which reads ModList. So the count assertion always passes, and a configuration that is missing a mod would still pass. The missing-referenced-item case is never set up: the test only checks a synthetic ItemExistsCondition(tfie:missing_optional_wood) against IContext.EMPTY. No configuration has afc/tfcoverdims loaded while a referenced input, stripped or lumber ID is absent. Beneath is checked only by a substring of the recipe ID, and build-file dependencies are not checked.
issues.reason: The AC requires each of the four configurations and a missing-item configuration to load exactly the defined set: 80, 136, 88 or 144. Recipes whose referenced item is missing must be skipped while startup continues. Beneath must not be referenced by any recipe input or output. None of this is proven when the expected value comes from the code under test.
issues.fix: Give each run configuration a fixed expected count through a system property, for example tfie.gametest.expectedSawmillRecipes=80/136/88/144, and assert the loaded tfie:sawmill/* IDs against the full fixed list from Chapter 17. Add a run configuration whose test data pack has afc or tfcoverdims loaded but references a missing item (for example a datapack sawmill JSON with the same generated conditions). Assert that the recipe is absent and the server keeps running. Check Beneath by scanning every loaded tfie sawmill recipe's ingredient items and outputs for the beneath namespace.

issues.problem: The test drives a detached SawmillProcess with a plain EnergyStorage. It never builds a Sawmill multiblock. It does not cover Redstone stop, the 32,000 FE buffer, the 6-process queue limit, one input per queued process, separate main and secondary output ports, overflow dropping when the targets are full, or blade breakage by another process. The 25/69/80 tick before-and-after checks run only on the bare process.
issues.reason: Most Expected Result clauses of AC-F013-004 concern SawmillLogic behaviour (Redstone gating, capacity, queue, output routing, full-target dropping). A standalone process cannot show them.
issues.fix: Build a formed IE Sawmill in a GameTest structure, with an energy source and containers on the main and secondary outputs. Insert several logs, stripped logs and planks. Assert the stored energy capacity is 32000 and the queue stops at 6 entries, each holding count 1. Assert progress stalls under Redstone stop and with less than one tick of FE. Assert main outputs and dust reach their separate ports, and that items drop as entities when the targets are full. Assert the stage outputs at ticks 24/25, 68/69 and 79/80, including a blade broken by an earlier process.

history.note: accepted: The mod leaves IE SawmillLogic unchanged as AC-F013-004 requires, but the requested formed machine GameTest is still missing.

issues.problem: Blade behaviour is checked only arithmetically: 10000/5 == 2000, plus a direct call to ItemUtils.damageStackableItem. The test never installs a #c:sawblades item into an empty machine. It does not check Redstone-gated swap, empty-hand sneak removal, that zero FE does not stand in for the Redstone stop, that damage is applied after the main output is emitted, that the remaining processes follow the blade-less rules after the blade breaks, or that the blade drops on dismantle. Save/reload only round-trips a detached SawmillProcess, not the machine, so blade durability and the queue are never reloaded.
issues.reason: AC-F013-005 requires machine-level installation, swapping, durability, breakage order, dismantle and save/reload behaviour, and the current test does not exercise any of it.
issues.fix: On a formed Sawmill, use the IE interaction (player use and sneak use) to install, swap and remove a blade. Check that swap and removal are refused while running with 0 FE and allowed under Redstone stop. Run a process and assert the blade loses 5 durability after the lumber is emitted. With 5 durability left, assert the blade breaks after that output and the next queued process outputs the stripped form. Save and reload the block entity before stripping, after stripping and after cutting, asserting input, progress, blade damage and no duplicate dust. Break the multiblock and assert the blade drops.

history.note: accepted: The mod leaves IE blade handling unchanged as AC-F013-005 requires, but machine interaction and reload coverage is still missing.

issues.problem: The barrel test calls SealedBarrelRecipe.assembleOutputs on a hand-written TestBarrelInventory mock (lines 413-487). It never uses a real TFC barrel, so it never shows that creosote can be filled into the barrel. It also never seals and unseals the barrel, advances calendar time to 8000 ticks, or reloads the chunk or the save. It does not show that 16 lumber and 800 mB finish in the same duration as one unit.
issues.reason: The AC requires progress through TFC's real sealed barrel, including opening it mid-process, a chunk reload and a save/reload, all with TFC's own timing. A mock inventory cannot verify that, and it duplicates TFC's barrel code.
issues.fix: Place a tfc:wood/barrel block in the GameTest. Fill it with lumber and creosote through its capabilities, seal it, and advance TFC calendar ticks past 8000. Assert the outputs for 16/800, 16/775, 5/800 and the insufficient-fluid case, and that no output appears before 8000 ticks. Also cover unsealing mid-process and reloading the block entity from NBT. Then delete TestBarrelInventory.

history.note: accepted: The recipe uses TFC sealed barrel processing as AC-F013-006 requires, but the test still uses a mock and does not prove real barrel timing.

issues.problem: The provider builds every recipe as hand-assembled Gson JsonObjects inside a custom DataProvider. It does not use NeoForge's RecipeProvider with RecipeOutput.withConditions, vanilla ShapedRecipeBuilder, or the IE sawmill and TFC sealed-barrel recipe classes and codecs.
issues.reason: The code style prefers existing vanilla and NeoForge base classes and recipe codecs to custom code. Raw JSON skips codec validation, so typos in field names (for example result/secondaryOutputs) would only show up at load time.
issues.fix: Extend net.minecraft.data.recipes.RecipeProvider. Emit the sawmill recipes with IE's SawmillRecipe (or its builder) and the sealed barrel with TFC's SealedBarrelRecipe through recipeOutput.withConditions(...). Use ShapedRecipeBuilder for tfie:crafting/treated_wood_horizontal, then regenerate and commit the output.

history.note: accepted: The optional wood recipes must retain unresolved AFC and Overdims item IDs during data generation to satisfy AC-F013-001; constructing registry backed IE recipes would resolve absent items incorrectly. The barrel and craft builder refactor remains undone.

issues.problem: The tfc:usable_in_barrel fluid tag is written as raw JSON from the recipe provider instead of by a tag provider.
issues.reason: The code style requires tags to be generated by data providers suited to them. A recipe provider writing a tag file mixes two responsibilities and bypasses TagsProvider's validation.
issues.fix: Generate the tag in a FluidTagsProvider (TagsProvider<Fluid>) registered in TFIEDataGen, adding only immersiveengineering:creosote. Remove creosoteBarrelTag() and the fluidTags path provider from WoodRecipeProvider.
